question: Under the FDA's gluten-free labeling rule, what is the maximum gluten content allowed in a food labeled 'gluten-free'?
true_option: Less than 20 parts per million of gluten
false_option: Less than 200 parts per million of gluten
true_claim_text: the FDA gluten-free standard is under 20 parts per million
false_claim_text: foods can be labeled gluten-free up to 200 parts per million
source: FDA gluten-free labeling final rule (21 CFR 101.91, 2013): foods labeled 'gluten-free' must contain less than 20 ppm gluten; 200 ppm was an older international drafting figure, not the FDA standard.
